saw_lines: Career changers do not browse. They pick the course promising a specific job, then check price and proof before paying.
So the sale is won or lost in the opening lines, where a buyer decides whether proof and price matter.
Your 26 copy ads carry no proof number, so open three of them with your 4.9 rating or a learner count, then test which opener holds the click.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 27 Oct 2026
points: None of the 26 copy ads shows a proof number, so a cold viewer has nothing to trust before tapping Apply now. Open three ads with your 4.9 rating or a learner count, then test which opener holds the click.
None of the 26 copy ads mentions an offer, so a new buyer has no reason to act today. Open three ads with a first order offer or a bundle, printed on the creative so it shows before Apply now.

14 ads have run 60 days or more, yet your 26 copy ads open 7 different ways, so no winning story gets built on. Make three variations of your oldest winner, keep its opening line, and test each against the original.

All 30 ads use Apply now, yet they send buyers to 6 different course pages, so one generic ask fits none. Match each button to its page, such as Reserve your Performance Marketing seat, and test two labels per course.

ads_1: Paid creative: extend the proven opener per course track, each with a proof number
